key: The highest excellence is like (that of) water.
s: The chapter likens the highest excellence to water, which benefits all things and takes the low place all men dislike; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 8, takes the highest excellence as a person whose nature is like water’s, and reads what follows as water’s ways, giving all things life, stopping when dammed and flowing when released.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 8, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 上善之人，如水之性。…萬物得水以生。…壅之則止，決之則流，聽從人也。
evidence.gloss: The person of highest goodness is like water in nature. … All things receive water and so live. … Dam it and it stops, cut it a channel and it flows: it goes along with people.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 8, at [7]); the Heshang Gong commentary glosses 上善若水 as 上善之人，如水之性 and then reads each line of the chapter as a trait of water (水性), including 萬物得水以生 on 與善仁 and 壅之則止，決之則流 on 夫唯不爭. One change to the sentence: “as a person with water’s nature” became “as a person whose nature is like water’s”, because the commentary says 如水之性 (like the nature of water), a likeness and not an identity. Wang Bi’s comment on the chapter is slight, so the Heshang Gong choice is sound. Corrected entry passes entry-check.
